sections.html:
Gary is a city in Lake County, on the southern shore of Lake Michigan, about 25 miles southeast of Chicago. Its shape is a T, with the northern edge along the lake.

The city covers about 50.7 square miles and sits at an elevation of 597 feet. It is the western gateway to Indiana Dunes National Park and contains the park's western portion, including Miller Woods. Soil about a foot below the surface is mostly sand, which companies have mined for more than a century, especially for glass.

Lake County is Indiana's second-most populous county, with 498,700 residents in 2020, and its county seat is Crown Point. Gary itself counted 69,093 people in 2020.

sections.h2: How did U.S. Steel create Gary, and what happened to its population?
sections.html:
U.S. Steel founded Gary in 1906 as a company town for its Gary Works plant, and the city was incorporated on July 14, 1906. It was named for Elbert Henry Gary, the corporation's first chairman.

MeasureFigure
Population peak (1960)178,320
Population, 2020 census69,093
Population, 2025 estimate67,289
Gary Works employment, early 1970sOver 30,000
Gary Works employment, 19906,000
Gary Works employment, 20232,246

The population has fallen about 61 percent since 1960. Lake County's steel employment dropped from over 60,000 in the 1960s to about 18,000 by 2015.

sections.h2: What other industries and projects operate in Gary now?
sections.html:
Heavy industry still anchors the economy, and Wikipedia describes U.S. Steel's Gary Works as the largest steel mill complex in North America. Two casinos opened on the lakeshore in the 1990s, and a $300 million Hard Rock casino opened in May 2021.

Gary/Chicago International Airport is an alternative to Chicago's two larger airports, with a runway inaugurated in 2015. The South Shore Line commuter rail runs between Chicago and South Bend, and the Gary Public Transportation Corporation operates local service.

  • Interstates: I-90, I-80, I-94 and I-65.
  • U.S. routes: 6, 12 and 20, plus State Road 912 (Cline Avenue).
  • The Cline Avenue bridge was closed for eleven years and reopened in 2020.

sections.h2: How many Gary houses are vacant, and how is the city responding?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 37,274 housing units in Gary, and 23.2 percent of them were vacant. The rental vacancy rate was 9.9 percent and the homeowner vacancy rate was 2.8 percent. A 2013 city estimate put about one-third of homes as unoccupied or abandoned.

The city runs a demolition program that targets unsafe structures. In a March 10, 2025 city release, Mayor Eddie Melton's office said 35 structures were demolished in Aetna in 2024 and over 20 more were planned there in 2025. Construction firms and the Lake County Highway Department volunteered their services. Before any demolition, the Department of Redevelopment reviews each property under Indiana's Unsafe Building Law, which includes identifying the property, notifying owners and assessing condition.

A separate city article on its citywide blight blitz said the campaign targets about 60 unsafe structures in Downtown, Emerson, Glen Park, Midtown and Westside. The March 2025 release added that the city was piloting a multi-department approach with smoke alarms, patrols and rodent abatement, and that Midtown and Emerson were due for more demolitions that year.

If you own a house that the city has flagged, respond to the notice. A flagged house can still be sold, but the buyer will want to know about the notice and any deadline on it.

sections.h2: Which Gary neighborhoods and school districts should a seller know?
sections.html:
Wikipedia lists these neighborhoods: Downtown Gary, Downtown West, Emerson, Ambridge Mann, Brunswick, Tolleston, Black Oak, Glen Park, Midtown, Aetna and Miller Beach. Broadway divides downtown into two areas, and Miller Beach is the easternmost neighborhood, bordering the Indiana Dunes.

Three public districts serve the city. The Gary Community School Corporation covers most of it, Lake Ridge Schools Corporation serves Black Oak and unincorporated Calumet Township, and River Forest Community School Corporation serves a small southeastern portion. Several charter schools also operate in the city, and Gary has closed 21 public schools, most of which remain unused.

sections.h2: What does lake-effect weather mean for a Gary house?
sections.html:
Gary has a humid continental climate, with July and August highs averaging about 84 degrees Fahrenheit and January and February highs about 29. Annual precipitation averages about 40 inches, and snowfall averages about 25 inches a year, with lake-effect snow common.

Vacant houses feel that weather first, since nobody is there to clear snow, watch for leaks or keep heat on. If your Gary house has been empty through a winter, document its condition with dated photos before you talk with any buyer.

sections.h2: What rules apply to rental properties in Gary?
sections.html:
Gary requires owners of residential rental units to register them each year under Ordinance C.P.O. 2012-79, and the Building Department's page lists the fee as $5 per single-family home.

  • For multi-unit properties the fee is $5 per unit, up to four units.
  • Enrollment runs from January 1 through March 30 each year.
  • Late registration adds $25 per property.
  • Noncompliance may bring fines starting at $250.

That page did not give inspection details, so ask the Building Department what applies to your property. City Hall is at 401 Broadway, with public hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Central Time, Monday through Friday.

sections.h2: How do Lake County taxes and the tax sale work for a Gary owner?
sections.html:
Gary property tax is paid to the Lake County Treasurer, at 2293 N. Main Street, Crown Point, IN 46307, telephone 219-755-3760. The county's online Tax Search page is the listed way to pay.

Indiana's Department of Local Government Finance lists May 11 and November 10 for 2026. A payment made within 30 days after a due date carries a 5 percent penalty if there are no back taxes, and it rises to 10 percent after that.

Owners who fall behind can face a tax sale. The county compiles a delinquent list on or before July 1 each year, or 51 days after the payment due date, and sends a certified letter to each owner. Names and addresses are published in two local newspapers. The sale is held entirely online within 171 days of certification, and the minimum bid is everything owed on the parcel. Unsold parcels go to the Board of Commissioners. The statutes are Indiana Code 6-1.1-24 and 6-1.1-25.

An owner who is behind can ask the treasurer for a payoff statement and weigh a sale before the certification date.

Any sale for money also needs a Sales Disclosure Form signed by both parties and filed with the county auditor after assessor review, with a $20 fee unless an exception such as foreclosure, divorce or probate applies.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Gary?
sections.html:
A Gary owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer, and the right choice depends on the condition of the house and the block.

  • List the house when it is in showing condition and you can wait for buyer financing.
  • Sell it yourself when you want to skip a listing fee and can handle the paperwork.
  • Ask for a cash offer when the house is vacant, damaged, inherited, behind on taxes or under a city notice.

We buy houses in Gary as they are, with a no-obligation offer.
